title: Meta Ad Limit per Ad Account: What Counts and How to Stay Under
summary: Meta limits how many ads a Page and an ad account can run, tied to spend. What counts toward the limit, the error you see, and how to clear room fast.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- Meta limits how many ads one **Page** can run at once, and how many ads, ad sets and campaigns one **ad account** can hold.
- The Page limit is tied to **spend history** : a new or low-spend Page can run fewer ads than one that spends heavily. Meta does not guarantee a fixed number for your account.
- Meta's developer documentation sets a ceiling of **5,000 non-archived ads per ad account** , with similar ceilings on ad sets and campaigns. Check the current figures before you build around them.
- Active and scheduled ads count. Ads in review count too. Paused or completed ads generally do not count toward the running total, but archived or deleted ones free up the account-level slots.
- To stay under: archive what is finished, consolidate near-duplicates, and test with dynamic creative or flexible ads instead of one ad per variation.


Most advertisers never meet an ad limit. Those who do tend to meet it at a bad moment: during a big launch, with 200 ads queued, and an error banner. Here is how the limits work and how to avoid them.


## There are two different limits


The messages look alike, but they are different problems.


Page ad limit Ad account limit


What it caps How many ads a Page can run at the same time How many ads, ad sets and campaigns the account can contain


What sets it Meta's rules on spend and account standing A fixed ceiling per account


What counts Active, scheduled and in-review ads Every non-archived, non-deleted item


Typical cause A new or low-spend Page, or a very large test Years of accumulated, never-archived ads


Fix Turn off or delete running ads, or build spend history Archive or delete old items


## The Page-level ad limit


Meta controls the volume of ads a Page can run so that new or untrusted accounts cannot flood the platform with ads. The principle is simple: the more you have spent, with a clean record, the more ads the Page can run. A brand-new Page starts with a low allowance, which grows as the Page builds a spend history. The largest advertisers can run ads in the thousands.


Meta does not publish a single table that applies to everyone, and the allowance can differ between Pages. Meta does not publish the number in a dashboard. If it matters to your plan, ask your Meta rep, or read the notice that appears when you reach it.


When you reach it, the typical error says you have reached the limit of ads that can run for the Page. It blocks publishing new ads until room opens up.


## The ad account limits


Separate from the Page, an ad account can hold only so many objects. Meta's developer documentation lists the ceiling as 5,000 non-archived ads per ad account, with comparable caps on ad sets and campaigns. Archived and deleted ads do not count against it. Meta can change these figures, so confirm them in its Marketing API documentation if you plan automation at that scale.


The account limit rarely affects a small business. It affects agencies that keep all clients in one account, ecommerce brands that spin up an ad per product, and teams that have created ads for years without cleaning up.


## What counts, and what does not


- **Counts toward the Page limit:** active ads, ads scheduled to start, and ads in review.
- **Usually does not count toward the Page limit:** paused, rejected and completed ads. A paused ad still sits in the account, so it keeps using an account-level slot.
- **Counts toward the account limit:** every ad that is not archived or deleted, whatever its status.
- **Dynamic creative and flexible ads** count as one ad, even though they hold many assets. That is the main reason to use them when volume is a constraint.


If your count looks wrong, filter Ads Manager by delivery status and make sure no "Off" or "Scheduled" ads from an old campaign are still lingering.


## How to stay under the limit


1. **Archive finished work.** After a campaign ends, archive it. This frees account-level capacity and keeps reporting clean.
2. **Delete clear losers early.** Ads with spend and no results after a fair run should be turned off, not left to sit.
3. **Consolidate variations.** Ten ads that differ by one word can be one dynamic creative ad with ten headlines. See[how to create multiple ads on Facebook](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/how-to-create-multiple-ads-on-facebook) .
4. **Use catalogs for products.** A catalog ad draws from a feed and does not need a separate ad per product.
5. **Stage launches.** Launch the ads you need in the first week, then rotate new ones in as the old ones stop.
6. **Spread across Pages when there is a real reason.** Separate brands and regional entities may have their own Pages, each with its own allowance. Do not create Pages only to dodge limits, since Meta can see the pattern and may restrict them.
7. **Keep spend history.** A steady, clean record helps the Page's allowance grow.


## What to do when you hit it


1. Read the exact error. It says whether the Page or the ad account is the problem.
2. In Ads Manager, sort ads by spend and delivery. Turn off the bottom performers.
3. Archive old campaigns.
4. Retry publishing. Counts can take a short while to update.
5. If the limit seems wrong for your spend, contact Meta support through Business Help.


## More ads are not the goal


Hitting the ceiling often means the account is testing too many things at once. Meta's delivery gives most of an ad set's spend to a few ads, so most of a large pile never get a fair run. A smaller set of distinct ideas, replaced on a rhythm, beats a large pile of near-duplicates. Meta's delivery changes have made creative variety, not volume, the thing that matters, and the[Meta Andromeda](https://www.sprites.ai/meta-andromeda) page covers why.


To judge your own volume, look at brands in your market. See how many different ads comparable advertisers run in the[Meta ads library](https://www.sprites.ai/meta-ads-library) , in industry pages like[fashion ads](https://www.sprites.ai/fashion-ads) and brand pages such as[Allbirds ads](https://www.sprites.ai/allbirds-ads) . Cost context is in[Facebook ads cost](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/facebook-ads-cost) .

## Frequently asked questions


### How many ads can I run on Facebook at once?


It depends on your Page. Meta ties the allowance to spend history and account standing, so a new Page can run fewer ads than a high-spend one. Meta does not publish one number for everyone.


### What is the maximum number of ads in a Meta ad account?


Meta's developer documentation lists 5,000 non-archived ads per ad account, with comparable limits on ad sets and campaigns. Archived and deleted items do not count. Confirm the current figure with Meta.


### Do paused ads count toward the limit?


Paused ads generally do not count toward the Page's running-ad limit, but they still count toward the account's object limit until you archive or delete them.


### Why does Facebook say I have reached my ad limit?


Either the Page has hit the number of ads it may run, or the ad account holds the maximum number of ads, ad sets or campaigns. The message tells you which. Turn off or delete ads, or archive old campaigns, then retry.


### Does a dynamic creative ad count as one ad?


Yes. It counts as a single ad however many images, texts and headlines it holds, which makes it a good fit when you are near a limit.


### How do I increase my Meta ad limit?


Build a clean spend history over time, since the Page allowance grows with it. If it looks too low for your spend, contact Meta support through Business Help.
